rationale: Both are short and correct. A keeps two parallel structures, a grade-to-names map and a separate enrolled-names set, which must be kept in sync to enforce the one-enrolment rule. It also returns a boolean from add_student that nothing in the interface uses. B stores a single name-to-grade dict. That one source of truth enforces uniqueness by construction, and roster and grade are simple sorted views over it, with roster sorting on a (grade, name) key exactly as the specification describes. A's grade-keyed map gives faster per-grade lookups, but that does not matter at this scale. B's single, self-consistent data model gives it a slight edge.
